column1: How many configuration memory bits does a 4-input lookup table (LUT-4) require, and why?
column2: 16 bits (2^4), one bit for each possible input combination, allowing it to implement any of the 2^16 = 65,536 possible 4-input Boolean functions.

column1: What key insight enabled modern FPGAs, pioneered by Xilinx engineers in the early 1980s?
column2: Any combinational logic truth table can be stored in a small SRAM; treating SRAM as a lookup table (rather than data storage) allows a memory block with n address inputs to realize any Boolean function of n variables.

column1: Why does FPGA routing/interconnect configuration memory typically consume more die area than the logic resources themselves?
column2: Because the routing problem demands extraordinary flexibility—dense wiring channels with switch boxes containing dozens of programmable pass transistors at every intersection to allow arbitrary connectivity between logic blocks.

column1: What are the three sequential operations performed by HDL synthesis?
column2: 1) Transform behavioral RTL into an intermediate DAG representation, 2) Logic optimization (collapsing redundancies, factoring, Boolean identities), 3) Technology mapping (covering the logic graph with actual FPGA primitives like LUTs, multipliers, BRAMs, carry chains).

column1: Define the 'critical path' in synchronous digital design and its relationship to maximum clock frequency.
column2: The critical path is the longest combinational delay between any two sequential elements (or input-to-register, register-to-output). Maximum operating frequency is the inverse of the critical path delay; no parallelism reduces this—only restructuring, pipelining, or faster process nodes can.

column1: What physical phenomenon occurs when setup/hold timing constraints are violated at a register input?
column2: Metastability—the register enters an undefined state with a nonzero probability of resolving incorrectly, causing statistically unpredictable production failures.

column1: Why is clock domain crossing (CDC) a fundamental reliability problem in digital design?
column2: Signals transitioning between clock domains with different frequencies or no phase alignment can violate setup/hold windows unpredictably, causing metastability; explicit synchronizers (e.g., double flip-flop synchronizers) are required to mitigate this.

column1: Why is exhaustive placement search intractable on FPGAs, using a 10,000-CLB example?
column2: A 10,000-CLB FPGA admits 10,000! possible placements—a number so large that evaluating even one configuration per nanosecond would take longer than the age of the universe, forcing heuristic optimization.

column1: What is the difference between global routing and detailed routing in FPGA place-and-route tools?
column2: Global routing partitions nets into coarse-grained channel assignments across the routing fabric; detailed routing then selects specific wire segments and switch matrix connections within each assigned channel.

column1: What hardened arithmetic components are typically integrated into a single FPGA DSP slice (e.g., Xilinx UltraScale+)?
column2: A 25×18-bit or 27×24-bit multiplier, a 48-bit or 96-bit accumulator, pre-adders, post-adders, and optional input/output registers—all hardened in silicon for throughput and power efficiency.

column1: What is the core invariant governing the use of specialized FPGA blocks (DSP slices, BRAM, SerDes)?
column2: Specialized blocks are not free: they impose hard constraints on interface standards, placement, and timing closure (e.g., DSP slices can't arbitrarily permute inputs without fabric logic; SerDes locks to specific GT sites; BRAM has fixed aspect ratios/port widths).

column1: What capability does Partial Reconfiguration (PR) add to FPGA systems, and what complexity does it introduce?
column2: PR allows swapping functional modules at runtime without interrupting other system components, enabling dynamic pipelines and adaptive accelerators—but requires static isolation boundaries and carefully synchronized handoffs between reconfigurable and static partitions.
